title: Access safeguards and SSO ops review with Northbound Capital
summary: Discovery-level security & operations review focusing on SSO onboarding, SCIM provisioning patterns, RBAC/least-privilege role mapping, audit log retention and KMS encryption questions. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Private deployment for regulated funds; primary concerns around certificate rotation, SCIM group sync reliability, and audit trail integrity.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Product); David (Northbound Security), Maya (Eng Manager), Tom (Platform), Priya (Legal)

--- Auto-summary (may be imperfect) ---
Redwood walked through SSO onboarding flow, SCIM provisioning options, and several RBAC patterns emphasizing least-privilege. Northbound flagged certificate rotation, audit log retention, and KMS key control as showstoppers for hosted plan. Action items agreed to exchange test metadata and map roles.

--- Transcript start ---
00:00 Alex (AE): Alright folks, thanks for taking the time. Quick round robin, say who you are.
00:07 David (Northbound): David Hsu, security at Northbound. Uh, we're mainly here to understand how Redwood will fit into our onboarding controls.
00:12 Maya (Northbound): Maya, engineering. I'll be running the integration with our identity provider.
00:16 Alex: Great. Samir, you want to take us through the SSO pattern?
00:19 Samir (SE): Yeah, sure. I'll keep it high-level first. Redwood supports SSO via SAML 2.0. Typical flow is IdP-initiated or SP-initiated, we expose an ACS endpoint and entity ID. You'll upload a certificate for signing that we rotate on a quarterly cadence unless you want custom rotation.
00:38 David: Quarterly? Hmm. For audit we usually need either customer-managed rotation or HSM-backed keys — rotation windows controlled by us. Is that supported?
00:45 Samir: Short answer: yes for Private deployments where you bring your KMS/HSM. For hosted we have a managed rotation and can set shorter validity on certs, but we cannot expose our key material. We can however integrate with your external KMS for data encryption at rest — that's a separate KMS bind.
01:02 David: Ok, so hosted doesn't let us rotate the SAML signing cert from our side, correct?
01:06 Samir: Correct, signing cert for the SP in hosted is Redwood-managed. You can enforce SAML assertion validation and we support verifying IdP signatures. If you need the SP key to be customer-managed, Private is the route.
01:16 Priya (Legal): Is there a documented key rotation playbook? We need to attach it to the vendor risk assessment.
01:21 Leah (CSM): I can send our key rotation and certificate lifecycle doc after this call — it's in our security pack. I'll also include SOC 2 Type II report.
01:31 Tom (Northbound): On SCIM, our HR system does group-based provisioning. How does Redwood map SCIM groups to internal roles? Do you support nested groups?
01:39 Samir: We map SCIM group->role via a simple mapping table. Nested groups are not preserved automatically; we flatten group membership during sync. If you rely on nested constructs we can add a sync hook.
01:50 Maya: Flattening is ok, but we need consistent deprovisioning. In some provisioning trials we've seen orphaned accounts. How do you guarantee timely deprovisioning?
01:58 Samir: We support immediate deprovision on SCIM delete events. There's a configurable reconciliation window as a fallback — default 24 hours. We can shorten that for strict enterprises to 1-2 hours in a private plan.
02:15 David: That reconciliation window is a compliance risk for us unless we get to 1 hour.
02:20 Alex: Noted. We'll mark that as an action item — Samir, follow up with what it looks like to shorten the reconciliation window.
02:26 Samir: Yep.
02:28 Maya: Also what about account locking and emergency revoke? If an admin is compromised, can we run a bulk revoke?
02:34 Samir: There's an admin console that lets you force session invalidation and revoke tokens. For larger orgs we have an API to trigger bulk deprovision or role swap. That endpoint is audited.
02:44 David: Speaking of auditing — what's in the audit logs? We need immutable logs of admin actions, role changes, and API calls with requester IPs and request bodies. Retention needs to be 7 years for our compliance.
02:58 Jordan (Product): Our audit schema captures user, action, timestamp, request path, and change diff for config ops. We store logs centrally and can push to an external S3-compatible bucket or SIEM via secure streaming. Retention is configurable on Private; hosted has default 13 months but extended retention is an add-on.
03:18 David: 13 months won't cut it. Legal requires seven. Is it possible to export logs for long-term archival?
03:24 Jordan: Yes, we can export daily archives to your bucket and you control lifecycle rules there. For hosted we recommend that for regulatory retention.
03:34 Priya: How do we assure immutability for those archived logs? WORM or object lock?
03:38 Jordan: If you use your own cloud bucket, you can enable object lock/WORM under your storage provider. We support signed uploads to that bucket with server-side encryption disabled so you own the encryption settings.
03:49 Priya: Good. We'll want that in the contract.
03:52 Maya: On RBAC, we want least-privilege. Do you have abstractions for permission boundaries — e.g., delegatable admin vs super-admin?
04:01 Samir: Yes. Our RBAC model supports roles with granular permissions. We support role hierarchies for UI convenience but recommend flat role-to-policy mappings for auditability. We also support attribute-based access controls on certain fields if you need conditional restrictions.
04:18 David: Can roles be scoped by project or tenant? We have fund-level isolation requirements.
04:23 Samir: We support scoping via namespaces — you can tag resources and restrict roles to namespace scope. That's how most fund customers set least-privilege.
04:32 Maya: Ok, and provisioning — do you recommend SCIM groups per role or per team?
04:36 Alex: Best practice we've seen is groups per role, then composition for team constructs. That way you can audit role membership directly from SCIM group membership.
04:45 David: How about service accounts? We need non-human service principals with long-lived keys but with rotation/usage constraints.
04:52 Samir: Service accounts are supported. They show as distinct principals in audit logs. Keys can be short-lived tokens via our token gateway. For longer-lived keys we recommend binding to your KMS and rotating using our key rotation cron or external secret manager.
05:08 Tom: Does Redwood have support for hardware-backed keys for encryption at rest? We run through FIPS boundaries in some of our audits.
05:14 Samir: Private deployments support HSM/KMS that meets FIPS and PCI requirements. Hosted can integrate with cloud KMS providers; if you need HSM-backed master keys exclusively under your control we'd recommend Private.
05:27 David: So if we go hosted, we still can enforce encryption at rest under our key?
05:31 Samir: You can supply a customer-managed key for data encryption with hosted via KMS integration in supported regions, but the SP signing cert for SAML remains Redwood-managed.
05:41 Maya: Can we scope data residency to specific regions?
05:45 Jordan: Yes, we have region tags for workloads. For sensitive funds we often recommend Private or Dedicated in the target region. Hosted has region availability but is multi-tenant.
05:57 David: Multi-tenant is fine if we get contractual assurances and logical isolation. We'll need encryption keys bound to our tenancy and network egress locked down.
06:08 Alex: We can put that in an addendum — network egress controls and key bindings.
06:12 Priya: Also on SAML: what NameID formats do you support? We use persistent NameIDs and custom attributes for entitlements.
06:20 Samir: We support email, transient, and persistent. We also accept custom attribute assertions; SCIM can populate groups with a custom attribute mapping.
06:30 Maya: For provisioning, our HR system doesn't push deletes reliably. How does your reconciliation handle soft-deletes?
06:36 Samir: We keep a reconciliation log and mark accounts as 'pending deletion' if we see a delete event fail. The default expiry for pending deletion is 7 days unless you configure otherwise. We can set that to 24 hours for strict policies.
06:50 David: Again, we need 1 hour.
06:52 Samir: Understood — we'll document where that config sits.
06:55 Alex: Quick question from me: do you have a preferred sequence for testing? Usually we set up a test tenant, run an IdP-initiated login, then push a SCIM create, and finally deprovision.
07:06 David: That sequence is fine. We'll want to see the assertion details and replay if possible.
07:11 Samir: We have a replay/debug console in the SE toolkit that shows raw SAML assertions and SCIM request/response payloads.
07:18 Maya: Nice. Will that contain PII? We have to mask SSNs and certain employee IDs.
07:24 Samir: Payloads in logs are masked by default for sensitive attribute names. You can opt in to unmasked for a specific debug session with an audit trail.
07:34 Priya: Any tokens or creds visible in those logs?
07:37 Samir: No, we scrub tokens.
07:39 David: Ok. Let's talk about emergency access and break glass.
07:43 Samir: We support break-glass roles. Access is gated with MFA, time-limited tokens, and elevated-privilege approvals. Every use of break-glass is logged and triggers an alert to configured owners.
07:56 David: That alerting — can it go to our SIEM and to our oncall Slack channel?
08:00 Jordan: Yes to both. We support webhook and syslog forwarding.
08:05 Tom: About SCIM rate limits — our HR system sends batches. Will you throttle and can that break sync cycles?
08:12 Samir: SCIM endpoints have rate limits to protect the system. We recommend batch sizes under 500 per request. If you expect higher throughput we can provision a higher rate for Private or Dedicated plans.
08:25 Maya: We anticipate quarterly onboarding bursts of thousands.
08:28 Samir: Ok we can design a burst plan.
08:30 Alex: We're coming up on the 10-minute mark. Should we pivot to mapping actual roles? Maybe David can describe a couple of common personas.
08:37 David: Sure. We have "Fund Admin" (full config access for a single fund), "Ops" (deploy and monitor only), "Trader" (query-only for market data), and "ReadOnly Auditor". We want to ensure "Fund Admin" can't access cross-fund secrets.
08:54 Samir: That maps directly to namespace-scoped roles. Fund Admin gets role restricted to a fund namespace, Ops gets deploy permissions but not secret read, Trader gets query/read access to market endpoints, Auditor gets read-only access to config and audit logs.
09:07 Maya: How do we handle cross-fund escalations for incident response?
09:11 Samir: You can create a temporary escalation role that is time-bound and requires two approvers; we log both approvals.
09:19 David: Will those approvals be visible in the audit trail?
09:21 Samir: Yes, attestation logs record approver IDs, timestamps, and justification.
09:27 Maya: Good.
09:29 Priya: On legal — do you support Data Processing Addendum and is that templated or negotiable?
09:35 Leah (CSM): We have a standard DPA and can add specific clauses for residency and subcontractor disclosures. Leah will send the current DPA after the call.
09:45 Priya: And insurance / breach notification SLA?
09:48 Leah: We include breach notification timelines in our SOC and contract. We'll highlight that in the security pack.
09:53 David: One technical nit — what's the SAML assertion signature algorithm? SHA256? SHA-1?
09:58 Samir: SHA-256 by default. We don't allow SHA-1 for production.
10:02 David: Good.
10:05 Tom: On performance, if we have heavy auth traffic, is the SAML handshake a bottleneck?
10:10 Samir: We cache validated assertions on short TTLs; that helps. For high traffic we recommend a short-lived session token from Redwood issued post-assertion to reduce repeated full SAML handshakes.
10:23 Maya: Are those tokens JWTs?
10:25 Samir: Yes, signed JWTs. We can rotate signing keys and publish jwks endpoints.
10:31 David: Do you support SCIM 2.0 filters? We want to sync on attribute filters rather than whole groups sometimes.
10:36 Samir: Yes, we support filter queries per RFC, and server-side filtering for better perf.
10:43 Alex: Timecheck — we have about 35 minutes left. Do you want us to demo the admin console now or save it for the SE pilot?
10:50 Maya: Save the demo. We want an SE-led pilot where we can run live SAML & SCIM tests.
10:55 Samir: Great. For the pilot we'll provision a sandbox tenant and grant Northbound admin access. We'll also provide a SE debug guide.
11:03 David: For the SE pilot, we will need to share our IdP metadata and a test user CSV. Who should we send that to?
11:10 Alex: Send to me and Samir, and Leah will CC security docs.
11:14 David: Expect a metadata bundle by Friday.
11:17 Maya: One more question on KMS: If we supply our own cloud KMS key and rotate it, how does Redwood handle re-encrypting existing blobs?
11:26 Jordan: We support envelope encryption. When you rotate the master key, we rewrap the data keys in the background. We keep the previous keys for a configurable window to allow rollbacks.
11:36 David: Is rewrap synchronous? We can't have a maintenance window that blocks production.
11:40 Jordan: Rewrap is asynchronous and rate-limited. We can schedule higher priority rewrap for an agreed migration window.
11:48 Tom: Will that generate a lot of I/O and cost?
11:50 Jordan: There's some cost — we'll include an estimate in the follow-up.
11:55 Alex: Recap time: action items, short list.
11:59 Alex: Samir to provide SCIM mapping template and reconciliation config options; Samir to document reconciliation to 1 hour option for Private. Leah to send SOC 2 and key rotation docs. Alex to prepare test tenant and metadata checklist. Northbound to share IdP metadata and admin personas. Any additions?
12:16 David: Add an item — we need a written assurance around audit immutability and how object lock will be enforced in the export pipeline.
12:23 Leah: I'll coordinate with product and legal on that and include in the security pack.
12:28 Priya: Please include breach notification SLA and indemnity language for our counsel to review.
12:33 Alex: Noted. Anything else?
12:36 Maya: Nothing more from engineering now.
12:38 Tom: We'll also give a sample HR batch to test SCIM throughput.
12:42 Alex: Perfect. We'll plan the SE pilot for week of 9/20. Samir, Leah, you'll lead the prep?
12:49 Samir: Yep. Leah: Yep.
12:51 David: Thanks everyone.
12:53 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the attachments and schedule.
12:56 --- End of transcript ---
